Fractured thumb, finger amputated, could miss six weeks

http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2518507-source-jpp-has-fractured-thumb-could-miss-at-least-six-weeks

New York Giants defensive end Jason Pierre-Paul had his right index finger removed Wednesday and a skin graft performed on much of his right hand and forearm, but the injury that could keep him out the longest is far more mundane.

According to a source with knowledge of the situation, Pierre-Paul has a fracture in his right thumb and may have other fractures in his remaining fingers and hand after a fireworks accident Saturday night. Pierre-Paul had surgery earlier this week on the hand to repair the fractures, placing pins in at least the thumb.

The source and two doctors with experience treating these types of injuries all agreed the fractures could keep Pierre-Paul from practicing for at least six weeks.

I like the vibe of this anime, badass Main characters that kind of do what they want. I've always enjoyed a bit of gang warfare style stories like this. Hopefully they can keep it up and I'll continue to enjoy it!

This is the first show in a while that had me speachless in the first episode. I can't really put a finger on why exactly I liked it so much. The art, the animation, the character, the music, all fucking great. The deaf guy, Nicolas, is by far my favorite character, he's amazing. When he slaughtere Barrys crew, goddamn. I loved it when he spoke in broken japanese. Oh and when he kicked the car.

If anything, Gangsta. is similar to Black Lagoon, another show which I really like.

In both shows we follow a group of criminals who basically work as a for-hire service hired by various criminal organizations to do jobs they either don't want to do or that the group does better. With this set-up we get a unique view of the underworld in these corrupt cities, where seemingly our "protagonists" are the only "moral" characters, but the character differences between the shows is what makes me think this show will steer off in a completely different direction than Black Lagoon. In BL we have a personality clash between the people in The Lagoon Company because of their different world views, which creates scenarios where we get to see how different people cope with their past and how they move forward because of it. Here, in Gangsta., we have two people who seem to come from almost the same type of background and who seemingly enjoy their work emmensly even though it's in a moral gray area, and it doesn't seem to faze them at all (just speculation since there's only one episode so far). That said; so far I really enjoy our protagonists and it seems like we will get to see their rise in influence in the city throughout this series.

I've not read the manga and I have no plans of doing so, so even though I speculate the future of the show I have no real knowledge on the matter. I look forward to seeing how this show will turn out, if it follows my predictions or maybe turns drama focused as BL.

As of right now Nicolas is my favorite character for the simple reason that his background is the one that interests me the most, I'm sure we will get a flashback of his past soon as it defines his whole character. There must be a reason he quit being a mercenary to join Benriya, and how he became such a killing machine even though being born deaf, ultimately missing the second most important sense to reading your surroundings in a fight, after sight. Not being able to hear a gun being fired outside of your field of view is detremental to your survival rate in a world where guns are the prefered weapon of killing.

Feels like I said the same thing over and over again, but I have high hopes for this series. If it keeps this up it'll be my favorite this season, maybe after Gatchaman Crowds Insight. but I havn't seen the first episode of that yet so Gangsta. is still in the lead.

If anything, Gangsta. is similar to Black Lagoon, another show which I really like.

As a manga reader, I like to describe Gangsta as a "Supernatural" Black Lagoon. If Black Lagoon took place in Gangsta's universe then every implausible thing Revy does would be explained. Just wait until they explain the Tags. I love Black Lagoon and this show is making me relive my love for badass adult MC's with a wonky moral compass! We need more of it!

I felt like the characters were really interesting, especially Nicolas being deaf. I think thats the first time I have seen an overtly deaf character that had to deal with the real world consequences of being deaf, specifically sign language. I really liked the world, and the supporting cast felt real, rather than just cardboard stand ins

Having said that, I thought the animation in the fights was a little off. Maybe I was just too spoiled from Fate last season, but there seemed to be a lot of iffy looking frames in the fight scenes, and some of them didnt flow very well. I only watched it once, so maybe I was just imagining it, but thats really my only complaint

One of the biggest fears that a smaller community has when there is any influx such as this is that the newcomers will drag in the crap the old users left behind, overwhelming the culture that everyone praised when they first arrived and that the old users molded.

So here's how we solve this problem. Think of voat as a giant vat of Awesome. When we have civil discourse, post OC, remind users not to generate low-effort content by leading by example, etc, we pour Awesome Sauce into the vat. However, for reasons related to Quantum Internet Theory, the vat has a slow leak at the bottom. Therefore, if we stop pouring the Awesome Sauce in, the vat will eventually be empty and there will be nothing left but garbage content, low quality pun comments, all that.

As we all know, it's possible to reach a point of no return. In the beginning, Digg was great, then not. In the beginning, reddit was great, then not. Right now in the beginning, voat is great.

If you dislike what you left behind and like what you've found here, then please, for the love of the goat, keep pouring in the Awesome Sauce. When we find other users not doing that, don't just downvoat (if/when we can), but let them know what's up. One might be surprised to find out that most people "shitposting" aren't really doing it on purpose! They just think that the bar for quality is that low or simply don't know at all. All we need to do is enlighten them. Can we do this?
The problem with other sites like this, beyond the people who moderate and run the site, was that its userbase started to allow low quality content to become prominent
